kind: C11 ellipticity and warped endpoint potential limits independently reconstructed
scope: Two directly reconstructed proofs of general C11 ellipticity and uniform finite-face convergence/normalized bounded pulled-back uniqueness in the fixed warped model.
mathematical_boundary: The finite disjoint power-stratum warped regime and its constructed base potentials. No general P15 closure, arbitrary endpoint potential uniqueness, pointwise convergence of balanced metrics, global C11 regularity upgrade or converse elliptic existence.

mathematics.method: Direct reconstruction from retained exact book foundations; no automatic theorem verdict

obligations.claim: Global C11 potentials have uniformly bounded measurable complex Hessian coefficients on compact X.
Positivity of the solution current gives nonnegative h-eigenvalues almost everywhere.
The retained C11 product identity identifies the ordinary top product with the measurable determinant.
A measure lower bound a h^n gives an almost-everywhere determinant lower bound a.
The compact coefficient bound gives a common eigenvalue upper bound K>0.
The product lower bound and the other n-1 upper bounds give every eigenvalue at least a/K^(n-1), including n=1.
An almost-everywhere positive matrix lower bound gives the same distributional current lower bound.
Finite unit-volume coefficient limits have b_j tending to b>0.
The right finite-face coefficients force v_j=c_j/e_j to tend to positive infinity.
The left finite-face coefficients force v_j to tend to -1/M from above.
Positive scaling psi_j=phi_j/b_j preserves supremum-zero normalization and kappa-plurisubharmonicity.
The interior base densities are exactly F_v sigma with F_v=1/(Q(v)(1+va)), and have integral one.
At the right end Q(v)=epsilon H_epsilon and F_v=1/(H_epsilon(a+epsilon)).
At the left end 1+va=f+ta with f=1-a/M and t=v+1/M>0.
The finite power-stratum hypothesis gives a common exponent 1<p<r for reciprocal integrability.
The extreme union has smooth volume zero; finite assignments there do not change any density measure.
H_epsilon tends to the finite positive H_a by dominated convergence.
Q(v) tends to the finite positive H_- at the left end by domination by 1/f.
The right and left density bounds are respectively C/a and C/f, with constants uniform near the end.
The p-th power domination gives strong Lp convergence to F_+ or F_-.
The strong Lp limits retain integral one.
The smooth positive compact ratio sigma/kappa^m converts the bounds to the fixed base volume convention.
The retained uniform compactness theorem applies to the fixed closed positive background kappa.
Every subsequence has a uniformly convergent further subsequence, preserving supremum zero and positivity.
Uniform bounded-product continuity and density convergence identify the closed equation of every cluster potential.
Closedness of kappa supplies both Guan-Li identities exactly.
The retained invariant-mass uniqueness theorem applies to the nonnegative Lp limiting density without an upper pointwise bound.
One cluster potential and compactness imply whole-sequence uniform convergence.
Positive finite b_j limits convert convergence of psi_j into convergence of phi_j and their holomorphic pullbacks.
Smooth coefficient convergence supplies a common local quadratic correction for every u_j.
Uniform convergence implies capacity convergence of the corrected bounded psh potentials.
Capacity continuity gives all corrected products weakly, with uniform local mass bounds.
The finite smooth-background expansion passes all ordinary products of degrees 1 through n to the limit.
The interior top products equal mu and their weak limit therefore solves the endpoint equation.
A bounded pulled-back endpoint solution has a positive horizontal base current by positive testing with w.
The submersion product expansion yields n L_0 A_chi^m=sigma as a base measure identity.
Off the extreme set the base measure is forced to be sigma/(n L_0).
The forced off-extreme density already has total mass H_0/n=b^m.
Closed bounded mass invariance gives total mass b^m for every competitor base potential.
Positivity excludes any extra mass on the extreme set, which is not inferred from mere cancellation by L_0.
The competitor chi/b satisfies the identical normalized closed-base equation and is therefore the same solution.
Neither arbitrary endpoint-solution uniqueness nor pointwise balanced-metric convergence follows from these arguments.
